core_mechanic: Not a mechanic: a distribution fact. Zero-install play is the growth channel, so the product problem is being findable inside it.
title: Distribution is the bottleneck, not the platform
why_hot: 2026 numbers: 15,000 HTML5 releases in H1 2025, Poki at 100m monthly active users, and developers naming discoverability rather than platform access as the reason to build for browsers.

audience: Habit players who open the same portal several times a day.
core_mechanic: One deterministic challenge per day plus a streak that only survives if the player returns.
title: Daily-ritual retention as the measured browser advantage
why_hot: Measured across 4.17 billion sessions in 2026: daily-ritual titles hold 40 to 50 percent of players at Day 7 and Day 30 while hyper-casual mobile loses 70 to 80 percent by Day 7.

audience: Students on shared laptops, siblings on a family desktop, anyone in the same room as a second player.
core_mechanic: Two players share one physical keyboard and one screen; one controls movement, the other aims, and a 60-second round ends in an instant rematch.
monetization: None on site; portal ad revenue is the surrounding model.
title: Same-keyboard 2-player local duels as the growth category
why_hot: 2026 portal search data: 2-player local titles run about 3x the session duration of single-player because every defeat asks for a rematch, and they need no accounts, no server, no lobby.
